analysis.title: GS What's Trending Across Credit 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: AI financing is the dominant credit theme: investors are discriminating between companies that can finance growth and those whose growth depends on financing staying available. IG cash widened ~3bps on the week while ORCL bonds and CDS moved 30-45bps wider.

September core CPI printed +0.33% MoM, a surprise to the upside, briefly sending the 10yr Treasury above 5.30%. Growth concerns and a tech selloff then drove a flight to quality, and 10s ended the week ~15bps lower at 5.07% while the Nasdaq fell ~4% and the S&P ~1.9%.

IG100 closed ~2bps wider on the week, but dispersion beneath the index was large. Oracle long bonds widened ~43bps to +320, Meta widened ~14bps, and parts of TMT saw 20-30bps intraday spread swings. Much of IG is still 3-5bps off the tights.

IG fund inflows were $1.06bn on the week, taking YTD to $240.6bn (~$101bn ahead of last year). IG supply was $28.9bn across 13 deals, YTD $1.92tn, ~25% above 2025. GS says the market offers limited spread compensation for macro uncertainty.

Bank earnings were a somewhat constructive start to the season (resilient NII, fees, manageable credit). Financials and insurance CDS were bid on concerns about AI-related investment concentration. Next tests are Industrials, Healthcare and Technology, where financing costs and capex could matter more. Lower all-in yields may temporarily slow yield-sensitive IG buying.
In leveraged finance, HYG fell 0.48%. CCC yields reached ~15.4% and CCC spreads breached 1,045bps, while BB demand held. Portfolio trading shows rotation out of CCC and stressed names into BBs.

CoreWeave (CRWV) was the center of the AI unwind, with its debt yield hitting 15%. Pressure spread across the data center ecosystem, and distressed and equity buyers of the debt appeared late in the week.

Single-name moves were large: JetBlue loyalty notes lost ~12 points after -10 the prior week (high-50s) on high oil prices. FMC bonds fell as much as 15-45 points after a guidance cut. UWM bonds fell ~5 points in one session before recovering. Acrisure bonds rallied more than 8 points.
Loans held up: higher-quality loans finished just 0.125-0.25 points lower. Loans have returned 2.99% YTD vs 0.27% for HY bonds. Loan funds took in $780mm on the week.

Duration rallied despite upside CPI and PPI surprises, as AI-related growth concerns and equity weakness outweighed inflation. With oil above $100, the question is whether weaker risk assets could constrain the path of Fed tightening.

Markets price about 5bps of tightening for the October FOMC. GS Economics expects an October pause followed by a December hike. The long end is caught between growth concerns, fiscal uncertainty and supply expectations ahead of the November refunding.

CDX flows showed focus on idiosyncratic downside. Decompression continued, with protection demand concentrated in HY and select single names, while generic IG indices were relatively insulated. Oracle CDS widened ~30-40bps. Macro accounts added hedges and real money stayed defensive, so the index is a less precise hedge.

GS GIR: USD IG and HY project finance issuance has passed $106bn this year, nearly triple 2025's full-year volume. GIR forecasts $300bn of global project finance issuance and another $420bn of direct hyperscaler issuance in 2027.

AI-related HY spreads widened 25bps over Oct 13-14 vs 2bps for non-AI credits. A sample of HY data center project finance bonds fell from an average price of $101.5 in June to $94.7 in October. Underwriting focus is on construction risk, refinancing, tenant guarantees, power availability and permitting.

GS Futures Strategies estimates CTAs are short ~$164mm DV01 globally, with potential buying of ~$20mm DV01 over the next week and $65-100mm over the next month in stronger rally scenarios, which could amplify a duration rally.

GS is hosting an AI Cross Cap Structure investor call Monday at 11am ET on the AI infrastructure selloff (semis, neoclouds) and what higher cost of capital means for capex. GS reports record nontraditional account inquiry on CRWV debt and ORCL CDS.

market_movers.rationale: Oracle bonds and CDS widened 30-45bps on the week, with long bonds +43bps to +320, underperforming Amazon and Google. Record investor inquiry on ORCL CDS.
CoreWeave debt yields hit 15% as the name became the AI unwind's beta barometer. Distressed and equity buyers of the debt appeared late in the week.
Meta bonds widened ~14bps on the week amid AI financing scrutiny.
JetBlue loyalty notes lost ~12 points after -10 the prior week, trading in the high-50s as high oil prices add pressure.
FMC bonds fell 15-45 points across the curve after a sharp guidance cut.
UWM bonds fell ~5 points in a single session before recovering amid rate-sensitive mortgage finance volatility.
Acrisure bonds rallied more than 8 points and loans ~7 points on dip-buying.

sector_views.rationale: Bank earnings were a constructive start, but financials and insurance CDS was bid on AI investment concentration concerns.
Tech credit saw the sharpest repricing on leverage, capex and financing risk. This is a description of credit moves, not a formal GS rating.
High oil prices are pressuring airline credits such as JetBlue. This describes price action, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: Money-center and regional bank earnings were a somewhat constructive start to the season, with resilient NII, fee generation and manageable credit performance (reported results, no figures given).
FMC cut guidance sharply, and its bonds fell 15-45 points across the curve (reported, no guidance figures given).
Upcoming earnings broaden into Industrials, Healthcare and Technology, where higher financing costs, persistent inflation and capex could prove more consequential (GS view, no estimates given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Upside surprise that briefly pushed the 10yr above 5.30%, but the yield then reversed lower on growth concerns.
Rally driven by AI-related growth concerns and equity weakness, despite upside CPI and PPI.
Market has largely priced out an October hike. This is a market-implied level.
The front end stays anchored by a Fed with inflation work to do.
Pressures airline credits and keeps inflation sticky.
Large supply pipeline tied to AI buildout.

risk_factors: Higher cost of capital for AI infrastructure and neocloud capex.
Persistent inflation with oil above $100 and a Fed still tilted toward tightening.
Structure risk in AI project finance: construction, refinancing, tenant guarantees, power availability and permitting.
Dispersion makes index hedges less precise, and jump-to-default risk is elevated in single names.
Liquidity deterioration in HY and CCC, with CCC spreads above 1,000bps.
Concentration of AI investment exposure in financials and insurers.
Treasury supply and fiscal uncertainty ahead of the November refunding announcement.
Tight IG spreads (3-5bps off the tights) offer limited compensation for macro uncertainty.
charts_described: IG100 vs 30Y Hyperscalers: hyperscalers underperformed this week and are now at YTD wides.
BB v CCC index spread to benchmark: CCC spreads hit 1000bps.
vol_and_positioning: IG100 closed ~2bps wider on the week while single-name dispersion was extreme. Parts of TMT had 20-30bps intraday spread swings.
CDX: decompression continued, with protection demand in HY and select single names. Macro accounts added hedges, real money stayed defensive, and hedge funds covered shorts.
Demand for short-dated IG protection was supported by jump-to-default concerns.
CTAs are short ~$164mm DV01 globally, with potential buying of ~$20mm DV01 over the next week and $65-100mm over the next month in stronger rally scenarios.
Positioning and YTD performance in HY drove a severe technical rotation out of lower-quality credit. Portfolio trading shows rotation from CCC into BB.
Fund flows (week / YTD): IG +$1.06bn / +$240.57bn, HY -$0.91bn / -$0.95bn, Loans +$0.78bn / +$17.65bn.

tension_points.bull_case: IG fund inflows of $240.6bn YTD and strong absorption of $1.92tn supply keep generic IG near the tights, with the index only ~2bps wider on the week.
tension_points.bear_case: Single-name dispersion is large (Oracle +43bps, TMT 20-30bps intraday swings), spread compensation is limited, and earnings broadening into Industrials, Healthcare and Tech could expose financing costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings in Industrials, Healthcare and Technology showing higher financing costs and capex pressure, or lower all-in yields slowing yield-sensitive IG buying.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth concerns and equity weakness pulled the 10yr down ~15bps to 5.07%, and CTAs short ~$164mm DV01 could amplify a rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Upside CPI and PPI, oil above $100 and a Fed that still has inflation work to do, with GS expecting a December hike and supply pressure ahead of the November refunding.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further deterioration in risk assets constraining the Fed's tightening path, or the November refunding announcement raising supply expectations.
